title: 15-Year-Old Erdogmus Climbs To World No. 15
summary: GM Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, the highest-rated 15-year-old of all time, is now world number-15 on the live rating list after winning a time-trouble battle on his 2026 European Chess Club Cup debut. GMs Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Anish Giri also won their first games as the favorites once again dominated, though GM Jorden van Foreest blundered and fell to a shock loss against 2409-rated IM Richard Pert. The European Women's Chess Club Cup saw the top teams clash in matches that could have gone either way. Top seed Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo beat second-seed Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica 2.5-1.5 after wins for GMs Aleksandra Goryachkina and Elisabeth Paehtz, while fourth-seed CE Gambit Bonnevoie overcame third-seed SuperChess Romania 3-1. 11-year-old WGM-elect Bodhana Sivanandan also starred with a win over IM Olga Badelka. Round four is on Tuesday, October 20, starting at 8 a.m. ET / 14:00 CEST / 5:30 p.m. IST. Although the level of opposition cranked up a notch in round three, the favorites still by and large cruised to wins. The one team upset in the top 12 matches, at least on paper, was 27th-seed SK Dunajska Streda holding 10th-seed Beer Sheva to a draw, though 16-year-old rising star GM Vaclav Finek beating 54-year-old GM Victor Mikhalevski on top board couldn't be classed as a surprise. Round three was the moment that teams mobilized their last reinforcements. Giri and Erdogmus had sat out the first two rounds for the top seed, but appeared for round three. As you can see, they both won, though the games were hard-fought. GM Sergei Movsesian, whose peak rating is 2751, lost his way in a tricky position, and Giri finished things off in style.

title: European Club Cup: Favourites set for direct encounters
summary:
Eleven teams remain tied for first place in the open section of the European Club Cup after three rounds, with tenth seeds Beer Sheva the only top-twelve team to have dropped a match point. The fourth round will see SuperChess facing Bayegan Pendik, with a potential battle between Anish Giri and Nodirbek Abdusattorov (pictured) on the top board. In the women's competition, Monte-Carlo and Gambit Bonnevoie are the only teams with perfect scores and will meet on Tuesday. | Photo: Gerd Densing

Open: Eleven teams remain on perfect scores

After three rounds, eleven teams share first place in the open section of the European Club Cup, all with 6/6 match points. The leading group includes all the teams seeded first through twelfth, with one exception: tenth seeds Beer Sheva Chess Club from Israel, who dropped a match point on Monday.

The Israeli team were held to a 3–3 draw by Slovakia's SK Dunajska Streda, the 27 th seeds. Interestingly, Dunajska Streda had a rating advantage on the top board, where 16-year-old Czech grandmaster Vaclav Finek was rated more than 100 Elo points above his opponent, Viktor Mikhalevski. Finek scored a win with the white pieces.

The Slovakian representatives were outrated on all five remaining boards, but Hungarian international master Aron Pasti also produced an upset by defeating Israeli grandmaster Eytan Rosen on board two. Beer Sheva secured victories on boards four and six, while the remaining two encounters ended in draws, leaving the teams with three points apiece.

SK Dunajska Streda v. Beer Sheva Chess Club | Photo: Gerd Densing

The other teams among the top ten seeds all registered comfortable victories, winning their matches by margins of at least 4–2. Top seeds Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club, representing Turkey, fielded their two highest-rated players for the first time in the competition. Both Anish Giri and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus contributed victories to their team's third consecutive match win.

Defending champions SuperChess Romania, the third seeds, also introduced their strongest player into the lineup. Nodirbek Abdusattorov, the highest-rated participant in the entire tournament, made a winning debut as the Romanian club maintained their perfect record.

Ediz Gürel (left) has scored three wins in as many games for top seeds Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club | Photo: Gerd Densing

Despite the favourable results for the leading teams, a few individual upsets occurred in the top matches. Richard Pert (2409), representing Cheddleton Savills Caterling, defeated Jorden van Foreest (2716) of SuperChess, overcoming a rating deficit of more than 300 points. Spain's Alvar Alonso (2560), playing for Silla Integrant Col-lectius, beat Nodirbek Yakubboev (2712) of Novy Bor Chess Club, while France's Pierre Laurent-Paoli (2550), representing Marseille Echecs, defeated Pavel Eljanov (2664) of Ashdod Chess Club.

The fourth round on Tuesday will feature direct encounters between some of the tournament's strongest teams. One of the most anticipated matches is the meeting between Bayegan Pendik and SuperChess, which could see Giri facing Abdusattorov on the top board. The individual board pairings had not yet been published at the time of writing.

Nodirbek Yakubboev suffered an upset defeat against Alvar Alonso | Photo: Gerd Densing

Women: Monte-Carlo and Gambit Bonnevoie still perfect

With only 22 teams participating in the women's competition, compared with 108 in the open section, the leading contenders have already begun facing each other. Following Monday's third round, two teams remain on perfect scores of 6/6 match points: top seeds Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo and fourth seeds CE Gambit Bonnevoie.

Defending champions Monte-Carlo secured a narrow 2½–1½ victory over second seeds Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica. Aleksandra Goryachkina and Elisabeth Paehtz provided the decisive victories for the Monaco-based club, while Stavroula Tsolakidou lost to Bulgarian international master Nurgyul Salimova, who participated in the 2024 Women's Candidates Tournament. The remaining game ended in a draw, allowing Monte-Carlo to maintain their perfect record.

Aleksandra Goryachkina | Photo: Gerd Densing

CE Gambit Bonnevoie, meanwhile, defeated third seeds SuperChess Romania by a 3–1 score. All four games were decisive, with Klaudia Kulon, Elina Danielian and Aleksandra Maltsevskaya scoring victories for the Luxembourg-based team. Nino Batsiashvili collected SuperChess' only point by winning her game on the top board.

The two co-leaders will meet in Tuesday's fourth round, with one of them potentially taking sole possession of first place.

SuperChess Romania v. CE Gambit Bonnevoie, with Nino Batsiashvili and Anna Ushenina on the top board | Photo: Gerd Densing

An eight-team group follows the leaders on 4/6 match points, with no teams currently on 5/6 match points. Among the chasing sides, the lowest-rated squad is Bulgaria's Velikova Chess Club, seeded 18 th . The Bulgarian representatives held higher-rated opposition to draws in each of the first two rounds before defeating Klaipeda on Monday.

Another notable result came from 11-year-old English prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan, who recorded her second consecutive individual victory in the event's third round. Representing She Plays To Win Lionesses A, Sivanandan defeated Olga Badelka of Gambit ASEE with the black pieces. The match finished in a 2–2 draw, leaving both teams on 3/6 match points.

Sivanandan is likely to face another considerably higher-rated opponent in Tuesday's fourth round, when the Lionesses take on SuperChess. The Romanian team's leading player is Georgian grandmaster Nino Batsiashvili, rated 2454.

title: Rookie Rachael Li Leads Women By Full Point; Wesley So Parries Fabiano Caruana
summary: GM Wesley So held onto his full-point lead in round nine of the 2026 U.S. Chess Championship by fending off defending champion GM Fabiano Caruana. There were five draws and just one decisive game, where GM Grigoriy Oparin defeated GM Sam Shankland to join Caruana in shared second place. The rest of the standings haven't changed. Rookie WIM Rachael Li leads the 2026 U.S. Women's Chess Championship by a full point after receiving a gift win against IM Nazi Paikidze in the form of a late endgame blunder. All six games were decisive among the ladies with wins by IM Tatev Abrahamyan, IM Carissa Yip, FM Megan Paragua, WGM Jennifer Yu, and GM Irina Krush against IM Rose Atwell, IM Anna Sargsyan, IM Anna Zatonskih, WGM Thalia Cervantes, and IM Alice Lee. That leaves Li on seven points—Krush and Lee on six. The penultimate round 10 is on Tuesday, October 20, starting at 1 p.m. ET / 19:00 CEST / 10:30 p.m. IST. Standings After Round 9: Open Round 9 Results: Open Nearly all six games were drawn in the open tournament, but it wasn't for a lack of fighting spirit. For tournament leader So, getting through Caruana was a critical mission accomplished on the way to potentially earning his fourth national title in the U.S. Round nine was a must-win game for Caruana, and when So sank into a 20-minute think on move six (in what's called the Dubov Gambit in the Italian Opening), Caruana's chances looked promising. "After he played b4, I literally wanted to resign, because I didn't expect this move at all!" said So, but he figured everything out over the board on his own. The star move was 11...a6, a novelty and a move Caruana thought would be hard for a human to find.

title: From quitting chess to becoming a Grandmaster - Interview with Arturs Neiksans
summary:
GM Arturs Neiksans looks back on his remarkable chess journey, from growing up in the small Latvian town of Valka and discovering chess at age nine to representing Latvia and eventually becoming a Grandmaster. He explains why he stepped away from competitive chess, how a career detour ultimately brought him back to the game, and how coaching, streaming and commentary became increasingly important parts of his life.

From quitting chess to becoming a Grandmaster

Interview with Arturs Neiksans

Arturs speaks about working with strong students, including Levy Rozman, his decision to skip the 2026 Olympiad, and why he is gradually shifting his focus from professional play toward commentary and content creation.

During his first visit to the ChessBase studio, he also recorded three new courses covering the Scandinavian with ...Qd8, the Alekhine Defence and the Chigorin Slav.
